newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: CRICKET-WALSH DESPAIRS OVER HIS PLAYERS' ATTITUDE.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-WALSH DESPAIRS OVER HIS PLAYERS' ATTITUDE.

text.p: Beaten West Indies captain Courtney Walsh openly despaired on Friday over his players' lack of commitment as they attempt to restore their credibility in the fifth and final test against Australia.
Mark Taylor's team have already secured the series 3-1 to retain the Frank Worrell trophy after West Indies slumped to their heaviest defeat in 40 years in the fourth test in Adelaide on Tuesday.
Walsh did not hide his disappointment over his players' attitude on tour, saying they had much to prove in the fifth test, starting on Saturday at the WACA Ground.
"We did not show enough hunger and we did not show that we wanted it as badly as the Australians did, that's why the scoresheet is the way it is," Walsh told reporters.
"I don't mind losing, but if you lose and you put everything into it and come off the field feeling you gave it your all but were simply not good enough, then I could live with that.
"But when you think there's still a lot you could have done and it just didn't happen then it's disappointing.

"Knowing deep inside you haven't given your best is cause for concern," said Walsh , who will almost certainly make his last test appearance on Australian soil in Perth, a favourite venue for West Indies in previous series.
While acknowledging Australia's superiority in the series, Walsh appealed to his players to show some pride in Perth to prevent a 4-1 defeat.
"Australia are playing the sort of cricket that we used to play," he said. "They've always played tough and hard but they've shown a lot more commitment than we have."
West Indies have beaten Australia in all four previous meetings at the WACA.
In addition to their pyschological problems, West Indies are struggling to overcome an injury crisis.
Wicketkeeper Junior Murray has a back strain and is expected to be replaced by deputy Courtney Browne, while fast bowler Cameron Cuffy and opener Adrian Griffith are also rated doubtful.
Australia, who leave for a tour of South Africa next month, named an unchanged side for Perth.
Australia (from) - Mark Taylor (captain), Matthew Hayden, Justin Langer, Mark Waugh, Steve Waugh, Greg Blewett, Michael Bevan, Ian Healy, Shane Warne, Andrew Bichel, Paul Reiffel, Glenn McGrath.

West Indies (probable) - Sherwin Campbell, Adrian Griffith, Shivnarine Chanderpaul, Brian Lara, Carl Hooper, Jimmy Adams, Phil Simmons, Courtney Browne, Ian Bishop, Curtly Ambrose, Courtney Walsh (captain), Robert Samuels.
